diagram_math_checks.objects: In the plane y=0, the given B is x^2+(z-2)^2 <= 1, with boundary circle centered at c=(0,0,2), radius 1.
diagram_math_checks.check: The drawn circle is centered at plot (0,2), radius 1, with z extent [1,3]; the origin lies outside with one unit of vertical gap. This follows directly from the Example and step 2.2.

P lies on the circle because 3/4+1/4=1. Its radial n has norm 1 and points out of B, not out from O. The dashed cP radius and outward arrow are collinear (plot uses rounded schematic coordinates 0.866 and 1.472).

diagram_math_checks.objects: Ordered oriented area vector psi_phi cross psi_theta.
diagram_math_checks.check: Step 3.1 gives sin(phi)(sin(phi)cos(theta),sin(phi)sin(theta),cos(phi)). At (pi/3,0), this equals (sqrt(3)/2)n, a positive scalar multiple of the displayed outward normal. This agrees with the local orientation definition, whose unit normal divides by the cross-product norm. The formula is well-defined at this seam parameter; no interior injectivity assertion is added.
